title: Introduce SLO-aware admission taper and localized echo backstop (hotfix)
author: Ava Morales
description: Motivation: during a recent regional surge we observed rapid circuit transitions that caused tenant oscillation and KPI spikes in tail latency. This hotfix implements an SLO-aware admission taper that gently reduces new fast-path admissions for tenants approaching their SLO credit threshold and a localized 'echo' backstop to preserve KV-cache locality during transient evictions. Changes: 1) new admission_taper policy that consumes per-tenant SLO credit metrics and applies a smooth taper curve instead of binary deny; 2) localized echo backstop that preserves a small prefix of KV cache and in-flight metadata for tenants that are transiently deprioritized to reduce cold-start latency on quick reinstates; 3) instrumentation: new metrics (admission_taper.rate, admission_taper.decision_reason, echo_backstop.preserved_keys) and tracing spans; 4) safety controls and rollout flags (feature_gate.slo_admission_taper, slo_taper.canary_percentage) and automated rollback if error-rate or tail latency regress beyond configured thresholds. Testing & rollout: unit + integration tests added; end-to-end perf run in benchmark-lab with synthetic tenant spike patterns; staged canary (5% traffic in us-west-2 for 2 hours) showed 18% reduction in p99 CPU spikes and no increase in error rate; full rollout performed with monitoring alarms and an automated rollback hook. Backwards compatibility & safety: default behavior disabled via feature gate; taper curve uses conservative defaults and a short warmup period; no breaking changes to API. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] perf run [x] canary signed off [x] telemetry and dashboards updated [x] rollout/rollback automation added. Related: references ENG-4267 and incident SUP-4482 for context.
